key: But among these there was not a man of them that were numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest, who numbered the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
s: Closing the census on the plains of Moab, the chapter sets it against the count at Sinai; Rashi, on 26:64, reads ‘not a man’ as the spies’ decree passing over the women, who held the land dear, and so the daughters of Zelophehad come next.

evidence.gloss: But among these there was not a man: but upon the women the decree of the spies was not decreed, because they held the land dear. The men said ‘Let us make a captain and return to Egypt’, and the women said ‘Give unto us a possession’; therefore the section of the daughters of Zelophehad is set next to this.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref Numbers 26:64 and at [142,64] match). Plain sense faithful: 26:63 closes the count by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab, and 26:64 sets it against the count in the wilderness of Sinai. Rashi on 26:64 says, in his own words, that the decree of the spies was not laid on the women, who held the land dear, and that this is why the daughters of Zelophehad follow; the sentence says exactly that and no more. Ibn Ezra and Ramban on the verse speak of the count and of Joshua and Caleb; they do not contradict. entry-check ok.
